title: Compatible local DVR diagram of a finite normalized compositum
statement: Let B and A be DVR domains [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with A a finite faithful B-algebra [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and let n be a natural number. Let E/Frac(B) be finite separable [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], with its compatible B-algebra structure. Set C=integralClosure_B(E) [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] and assume C finite over B. Suppose every prime R of C above m_B has ramification index e_R a unit in B, e_R dividing n, and separable residue-field extension k(R)/k(R intersect B); here k(R) is the residue field of C_R. Let F be a field and an A-algebra, and let i:E->F be a ring homomorphism agreeing with B->A->F on B. Assume F is generated as an A-algebra by i(E). Set S=integralClosure_A(F), assumed finite over A. Let Q be a prime of S above m_A. Then there is a prime R of C such that, writing U=C_R and T=S_Q [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], the canonical map B->U is local, both U and T are DVRs, E has a U-algebra structure making it the fraction field of U compatibly with B, and F has a T-algebra structure making it the fraction field of T compatibly with A. There is a local ring homomorphism j:U->T agreeing on B with B->A->T and satisfying U->T->F=U->E->F. Furthermore e_R is a unit in B, e_R divides n, m_B U=m_U^(e_R), and the induced extension (U/m_U)/(B/m_B) is separable. No condition m_B A=m_A^n, nor any conclusion about the residue extension of T/A, is asserted.

proof.text: Injectivity of the field map i and fraction-field injectivity imply B->F is injective. The kernel of A->F contracts to zero in B; integrality and the domain A force that kernel to be zero. Algebraicity of E over B descends from Frac(B); transfer through i and extend the coefficient ring to A. Generation then makes every element of F algebraic over A. Thus S has fraction field F.

S is finite over the Noetherian ring A, is normal in F, and has dimension at most one by integrality. It is therefore Dedekind. The prime Q is nonzero since its contraction is m_A. Apply the Dedekind localization DVR theorem to get T=S_Q.

Restrict i to C. Integral elements over B map to integral elements over A, defining i_C:C->S. Put R=i_C^{-1}(Q). Compatibility and locality of the integral faithful map B->A show R contracts to m_B. Finite separable normalization makes C Dedekind, and R is nonzero. Apply the Dedekind localization theorem to U=C_R.

Use Localization.mapToFractionRing for U->E and T->F. Their fraction-field and tower identities follow from the localization APIs. Define j by Localization.localRingHom R Q i_C; it is local. Its compatibility on B follows from the structural maps, and compatibility into F follows from localization ring-hom extensionality.

Every nonzero ideal of U is a power of its maximal ideal. Apply this to m_B U. The definition of R.ramificationIdx B is the length of U/(m_B U), and the DVR quotient-length formula identifies the exponent with that index. The input tameness gives its unit and divisibility properties.

The prime residue field k(R) is definitionally the local residue field of U. Put p=R intersect B=m_B. The canonical map B/p->k(p) is bijective. Compose its inverse with the quotient equivalence B/p=B/m_B. Transport the given separability through that field equivalence and the identity on k(R); compatibility is checked on the surjective image of B. This yields exactly the residue algebra from the local B->U map.

lean.statement:
theorem dvr_normalized_compositum_local_diagram
    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [IsDiscreteValuationRing B]
    (n : ℕ)
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    [Algebra B A] [Module.Finite B A] [FaithfulSMul B A]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (FractionRing B) E]
    [Algebra B E] [IsScalarTower B (FractionRing B) E]
    [FiniteDimensional (FractionRing B) E] [Algebra.IsSeparable (FractionRing B) E]
    [Module.Finite B (integralClosure B E)]
    (htame : ∀ (R : Ideal (integralClosure B E)) (hR : R.IsPrime),
      letI := hR
      R.comap (algebraMap B (integralClosure B E)) = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B →
      letI := Localization.AtPrime.algebraOfLiesOver (R.under B) R
      IsUnit (R.ramificationIdx B : B) ∧ R.ramificationIdx B ∣ n ∧
        Algebra.IsSeparable (R.under B).ResidueField R.ResidueField)
    (F : Type u) [Field F] [Algebra A F]
    (iE : E →+* F)
    (hcomm : ∀ b : B, iE (algebraMap B E b) =
      algebraMap A F (algebraMap B A b))
    (hgen : Algebra.adjoin A (Set.range iE) = ⊤)
    [Module.Finite A (integralClosure A F)]
    (Q : Ideal (integralClosure A F)) [Q.IsPrime]
    (hQ : Q.comap (algebraMap A (integralClosure A F)) = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) :
    ∃ (R : Ideal (integralClosure B E)) (hR : R.IsPrime),
    letI := hR
    let U := Localization.AtPrime R
    let T := Localization.AtPrime Q
    ∃ (hBU : IsLocalHom (algebraMap B U))
      (_hU : IsDiscreteValuationRing U) (_hT : IsDiscreteValuationRing T)
      (aUE : Algebra U E),
    letI := aUE
    ∃ (_hfracUE : IsFractionRing U E) (_hBUE : IsScalarTower B U E)
      (aTF : Algebra T F),
    letI := aTF
    ∃ (_hfracTF : IsFractionRing T F) (_hATF : IsScalarTower A T F)
      (j : U →+* T),
      IsLocalHom j ∧
      (∀ b : B, j (algebraMap B U b) = algebraMap A T (algebraMap B A b)) ∧
      (∀ c : U, algebraMap T F (j c) = iE (algebraMap U E c)) ∧
      IsUnit (R.ramificationIdx B : B) ∧ R.ramificationIdx B ∣ n ∧
      (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B).map (algebraMap B U) =
        IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal U ^ R.ramificationIdx B ∧
      letI := hBU
      Algebra.IsSeparable (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B) (IsLocalRing.ResidueField U)
